nodes.summary: The Minesweeper consistency decision problem accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a Minesweeper instance that is well formed and feasible, that is, admits a mine placement consistent with all of its clues. It rejects every bitstring that does not decode to a Minesweeper instance.
nodes.title: Minesweeper consistency as a decision problem

nodes.summary: Index rows and columns by natural numbers, and call a cell $(r', c') \ne (r, c)$ a neighbour of $(r, c)$ when $|r' - r| \le 1$ and $|c' - c| \le 1$. A Minesweeper instance with $R$ rows, $C$ columns and a list of clues is feasible when there is a finite set $M$ of cells $(r, c)$ with $r < R$ and $c < C$ (the mines) such that for every clue $(r, c, k)$ in the list the cell $(r, c)$ is not in $M$ and exactly $k$…
nodes.title: Feasible Minesweeper instances

nodes.summary: A Minesweeper instance consists of a number of rows $R$, a number of columns $C$ and a finite list of clues, where $R$ and $C$ are natural numbers and each clue is a triple $(r, c, k)$ of natural numbers giving a row $r$, a column $c$ and the number $k$ shown.
nodes.title: Minesweeper instances

nodes.summary: The Minesweeper consistency decision problem lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: MINESWEEPER CONSISTENCY is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A Minesweeper instance with $R$ rows, $C$ columns and a list of clues is well formed when every clue $(r, c, k)$ in the list satisfies $r < R$, $c < C$ and $k \le 8$.
nodes.title: Well-formed Minesweeper instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
